name: Kit Porter
life: “I still remember drumming on every tall step before school.” People around the downtown fountain know Kit by a small Sunday habit. Kit keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I played scales while the adults argued. By the time they stopped, I could play with both hands.
appearance: Kit is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a charcoal zip cardigan with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Kit draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
personality: Kit is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To learn the landing tune with both hands.
family: Rowan Armas is Kit’s stepsibling. A lost family paycheck once turned up in the lining of a coat. Their relatives still describe that week by the three people who quietly extended credit. Kit would rather forgive a debt than make a friend cross the street. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Rowan says, “I wanted an elegant beach photograph. The patch in the background is the one thing my mother recognized.”
connections: Amanda Hart. A breakfast listener gives the child an unhurried first audience.

reactions.situation: The owner asks a child to play first
reactions.response: Kit finds a steady seat for the child and waits for the opening notes.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Kit suggests one straightforward message without accusations and gives the friend time to answer.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Kit thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
